title: Experimental Kuramoto Platform
authors: Leandro Freitas, Victor H. S. Bittencourt, Débora D. Superbi, Wanderley C. Silva Junior, Arthur N. Montanari, Luis A. Aguirre
abstract: Phase reduction provides a principled relationship between high-dimensional oscillator dynamics and low-dimensional phase models such as the Kuramoto model. However, connecting analytical results derived from the Kuramoto framework to experimental data remains an open challenge, as many physical platforms violate the weak-coupling assumptions underlying standard phase reduction. Here, we present an experimental platform based on electronic quadrature oscillators whose phase dynamics are, under certain assumptions, equivalent to the Kuramoto model. Crucially, this equivalence is achieved for both weak and strong coupling through a non-diffusive coupling circuit, and the design approach supports arbitrary (weighted and directed) network topologies while preserving scalability and oscillation regularity. Across different coupling schemes, we demonstrate that the platform reliably reproduces phase transitions predicted by the Kuramoto model for both global and cluster synchronization. This cost-effective platform enables systematic experimental validation of analytical and numerical results for synchronization in complex networks.
summary: The authors present an experimental platform built from electronic quadrature oscillators designed to model coupled oscillator systems governed by the Kuramoto model. By employing a novel non-diffusive coupling circuit, they successfully demonstrate that their hardware can accurately reproduce phase transitions and synchronization behaviors across both weak and strong coupling regimes. This offers a cost-effective tool for systematically validating complex theoretical models of collective dynamics.
main_problem: Connecting analytical results from the Kuramoto model, derived via phase reduction, to experimental data is challenging because many physical platforms violate the weak-coupling assumptions.
main_result: The proposed electronic platform successfully reproduces Kuramoto model dynamics for both weak and strong coupling regimes across various network topologies.
method: The authors designed an experimental circuit using electronic quadrature oscillators coupled via a novel non-diffusive architecture to map oscillator dynamics onto the required sinusoidal phase coupling.
model_or_system: The system uses electronic quadrature oscillators whose phase dynamics are engineered to mimic the Kuramoto model ($\dot{\phi}_i = \omega_i + K \sum A_{ij} \sin(\phi_j - \phi_i)$). The coupling is achieved using external currents in a non-diffusive circuit.
key_observables: Phase coherence, order parameter (R), and observation of phase transitions (global and cluster synchronization).
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($K$), network topology (e.g., ring, all-to-all, directed), frequency mismatch ($\Delta\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The platform aims to achieve equivalence without relying on conventional weak-coupling phase-reduction assumptions; however, the initial coupling implementation is noted as being inherently diffusive.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate validation of synchronization transitions for different topologies (symmetric, all-to-all, ring, directed) and illustrate the $(K, \gamma)$-phase diagram for cluster synchronization.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical challenge, details the quadrature oscillator platform and non-diffusive coupling circuit, demonstrates its ability to reproduce Kuramoto phase transitions across various regimes, and concludes by outlining future extensions like implementing signed networks or adaptive control.
why_interesting: This work provides a tangible, low-cost hardware testbed for complex collective dynamics models (like Kuramoto), allowing experimental validation of theoretical predictions in parameter regimes previously inaccessible due to weak-coupling assumptions.
